Strategic Impact

Why This Matters for Your Team

Unified Account Planning unlocks three leader-level outcomes

Land each pillar in your own words. Unified Team Visibility replaces fragmented systems with one real-time view across Sales, CX, and Splunk so you stop chasing updates and start making decisions. Data-Driven Coaching is the shift from “checking in” to “coaching up” — AI surfaces the specific guidance that raises plan quality and focuses sellers on the right activities. Drive Growth is what it unlocks: a standardized approach where every plan is built for success and the team moves from reactive tasks to proactively capturing expansion.

01

Champion AI-driven insights

From Compliance check
“Did you use the tool?”
A yes/no answer that tells you nothing about the account.
Click →
To Strategic curiosity
“What did the AI summary reveal about the customer that we hadn’t considered?”
A question that surfaces strategy, sharpens the plan, and signals you trust the platform.
Mindset
Insights drive decisions
Strategic decisions must be grounded in the insights available in the platform.
Action
Treat AI as a partner
Encourage the team to treat AI as a partner, not a task.
This is the “how” behind Imperative 1. Land the Know, Say, Do framing: leaders need to know that strategic decisions must be grounded in available insights; they need to change the questions they ask in 1:1s from compliance (“did you use it”) to curiosity (“what did it reveal”); and they need to model treating AI as a partner. Then point to the specific features — AI Summary Generation, Recent News, and the thumbs up/down feedback loop — so the team knows exactly where to engage. Reinforce that their feedback is what makes the AI smarter every quarter.

02

Define What Good Looks Like

Define what good looks like in their own words. Land, Adopt, Expand, Renew is the rhythm of modern customer success. Click into the next view to coach the team on the difference between business objectives and the technical initiatives that deliver them.
02

What Good Looks Like

01
Objectives
What Good Looks Like
Written from the customer’s perspective, measurable, and validated by a customer sponsor.
Who
Account Owners
How
Define 2–3 core customer priorities
Coaching Question
“What are the top 3 business objectives, and what evidence supports this?”
02
Customer Initiatives
What Good Looks Like
Every initiative has a clear owner, a defined path, is documented in the “Value Definition” tab in SalesMain, and is directly linked to driving new or expanded pipeline opportunities.
Who
Architecture AEs & SEs
How
Translate objectives into technical initiatives
Coaching Question
“How does this technical solution directly support the business objective identified?”
Coaching Example From Vendor-Speak to Customer Outcome
Obtain SD-WAN business
Lower TCO and improve budget predictability
Win calling RFP
Improve employee productivity through omnichannel capabilities
Modernize edge compute
Reduce latency for critical edge apps to under 100 ms to improve customer satisfaction and conversion
Two layers of the plan, two distinct coaching conversations. Business Objectives are owned by the Account Owner and must be customer-perspective, measurable, and validated by a sponsor. Business Initiatives are owned by Architecture AEs and SEs and must trace back cleanly to a stated objective. The coaching question on each side is the test — if the seller can answer it crisply, the plan is in good shape.
03

Drive Strategic Agility

From Periodic check-the-box activity
“Have you completed your plan?”
A one-time deliverable that goes stale the moment the market moves.
Click →
To Dynamic asset that drives growth
“What has changed in the customer’s business since our last review — and how are we updating the strategy to reflect that?”
A living plan that adapts to change and proactively captures expansion opportunities.
Mindset
Planning is a growth engine
Evolve our planning process into a dynamic growth engine — one that adapts to market shifts, proactively captures expansion opportunities, and uses feedback to strengthen customer relationships.
Action
Schedule regular account reviews
Use the Internal Account Review deck to refine and adjust account strategy on a recurring cadence.
Imperative 3: Drive Strategic Agility. Shift the team away from treating account planning as a one-time exercise. The plan is a living asset — we revisit it, pressure-test it against what has actually changed in the customer’s business, and update the strategy accordingly. The action is concrete: schedule regular account reviews using the Internal Account Review slide deck so refinement becomes a habit, not an event.
